actions: inspected Replay Gap branching implementation, pilot configuration, and replay-fidelity machinery
inspected TraceElephant bundled SWE-Agent replay runner
searched public literature for strict rollback-target selector comparisons and inference-state rollback systems
derived minimum strict selector-only SWE-bench factorial and identified depth-dependent budget and return-code-only fidelity confounds
persisted new clean checkpoint and advanced own LATEST pointer
new_findings: Replay Gap already provides fresh-container prefix replay, arbitrary prefix continuation, multiple fork points and same-model controls, making it the strongest first substrate for the missing selector-only software-agent experiment.

Current Replay Gap branch accounting ties remaining calls to fork depth via resumed n_calls under a global step limit, so strict selector comparison must equalize post-intervention budget independently of rollback depth.
Current replay fidelity checks return codes; strict branch admission should also verify reconstructed workspace/repository state digest.

TraceElephant SWE-Agent run_replay reconstructs fresh environment behavior by replaying stored actions with ReplayModelConfig, but does not yet supply arbitrary-prefix replay followed by live continuation.
scope_guard: No result in this run establishes selector superiority. The strict factorial remains unlocated: same alarm, candidate set, restore/carry-forward, model and post-intervention budget with only historical target selector varied and final task success measured. SWE-bench container evidence does not establish irreversible external-effect safety.
exact_next_action: Search learned historical rollback-target selectors that can be plugged into a fixed Replay Gap candidate set; prioritize studies normalizing post-rollback action/token budgets and then inspect full inference-state restoration/cache-rebinding mechanisms suitable for identical live branches.
